summary: This extension of EffectiveBounds constructs small integer equations whose Jacobian-open rational scheme has a given number field as an irreducible component. It combines independent short integers, bounded first-jet parameters, saturated relation lattices and successive minima, then enumerates the resulting coefficient boxes to prove a field-count bound with discriminant exponent cubic in the logarithm of the degree.

nodes.title: Canonical Minkowski measure
nodes.statement: For a number field K with signature (r₁,s), on Mathlib’s mixedEmbedding.mixedSpace K put μcan = 2^s times its native product Haar measure. It is the volume measure of the real inner product Σρ xρyρ + 2Σσ Re(xσ conjugate(yσ)). The gauge g is the native coordinate supremum norm, not the norm of that inner product.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Each complex plane has metric matrix 2I₂ and volume factor 2; each real coordinate has factor 1. Transport the product Haar measure, preserving the separate supremum gauge.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The weighted real metric and supremum unit body determine the extra factor 2 per complex place; this node expresses it relative to the native product measure.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.canonicalMeasure_apply
api.statement: For any measurable set U, μcan(U)=2^s volume(U).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.canonicalMeasure_haar

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.canonicalMeasure_unitBody

nodes.title: Discriminant covolume
nodes.statement: The mixed-embedding integer lattice has μcan-covolume √|disc K| = δ^(n/2), where n=[K:ℚ]≥1 and δ=|disc K|^(1/n)≥1.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Read the native product-measure formula 2^(−s)√|disc K|, multiply the measure by 2^s, and use discr_ne_zero and the real-power laws. The result is not the unscaled product covolume.
acceptance: For an imaginary quadratic field the product-measure and canonical covolumes differ by 2.

sources.match: The embeddings Gram determinant equals the absolute discriminant; rescaling the native mixed-embedding covolume gives the canonical one.

nodes.title: Short first-half integers
nodes.statement: There are n algebraic integers ωᵢ, linearly independent over ℚ, with nondecreasing houses hᵢ≥1 and ∏hᵢ≤δ^(n/2). With m=floor(n/2)+1, every i<m satisfies hᵢ≤δ. These are simultaneous successive-minimum witnesses, not a chosen integral basis.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Identify the native mixed space with Euclidean real coordinates by multiplying each complex coordinate by √2. The real determinant is 2^s, so Euclidean volume pulls back to μcan. Transport the native supremum unit body and the integer lattice along this linear equivalence; the body remains compact, convex, centrally symmetric and has zero in its interior. Apply GN.1’s second theorem and simultaneous independent minimum witnesses to that body, then transport back. This preserves the supremum gauge rather than replacing it by Euclidean length.
The unit-body volume is at least 2^n, giving the product bound. Nonzero integral elements have house≥1. The ordered-product bound gives hᵢ≤δ^(n/(2(n−i))); for i<floor(n/2)+1 the exponent is≤1.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The second-minimum product estimate and the ordered norm argument bound the first floor(n/2)+1 independent integers by δ.

nodes.title: Products of a large subspace
nodes.statement: For any finite-dimensional field extension K/k and k-subspace V⊆K with 2 dimₖV>[K:k], the k-span of {ab:a,b∈V} is all of K. No separability or integral-basis assumption is required.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: If the product span is proper, choose a nonzero k-linear functional f annihilating it. The form (a,b)↦f(ab) is nondegenerate since K is a field: a≠0 and f(c)≠0 permit b=c/a. Thus V injects into its annihilator of dimension n−dimV, contrary to 2dimV>n.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The functional-on-products argument rules out a proper product span for a subspace of dimension above n/2; this node states its general field-extension form.

nodes.title: Short independent algebraic integers
nodes.statement: Every degree-n number field has n ℚ-linearly independent algebraic integers αᵢ with house(αᵢ)≤δ², hence |τ(αᵢ)|≤δ² for every embedding τ:K→ℂ. This is not a claim that they form a ℤ-basis of 𝓞 K.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Take the span of the first m integers from firstHalfMinima. productSpan shows its products span K; choose n independent products. Products are integral and the house is submultiplicative.
acceptance: For ℚ the one-element family (1) satisfies the bound.
Do not use the short family as the integral basis in the discriminant determinant.

shortIntegers_nonBasis: In K=ℚ(i) the family (1,2i) is rationally independent and has houses 1,2≤δ²=4, but its integral span has index 2 in 𝓞 K; it must be accepted by the theorem without being labeled an integral basis.

sources.match: Proposition 1 asserts n independent integers with all conjugates bounded by δ²; the proof selects products rather than an integral basis.

nodes.title: Integral parameter tuples
nodes.statement: For α:Fin n→𝓞 K and u:Fin n→Fin r→ℤ, define κⱼ=Σᵢ uᵢⱼαᵢ in 𝓞 K. The construction admits arbitrary signed integer parameters; the existence theorem chooses parameters in the inclusive box 0≤uᵢⱼ≤dn(r+1).
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native ℤ-module structure of the ring of integers and finite sums.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The short integers are combined using rational-integer parameters in r columns.

nodes.title: Bounded full-jet parameters
nodes.statement: Let n=[K:ℚ], r≥1,d≥5 and M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1). For an independent integral family α with houses≤δ² there exist parameters 0≤uᵢⱼ≤B=dn(r+1) for which the distinct embedding points Pτ=(τκⱼ) have surjective degree-≤d first-jet evaluation over ℂ. Every |τκⱼ|≤n²d(r+1)δ².
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: The embeddings matrix of the ℚ-basis α is invertible. On each of the r columns it gives an invertible linear change from parameters to point coordinates. Pull back a nonzero generic jet minor supplied by GI.5; its polynomial is nonzero and each parameter degree≤dn(r+1). Apply the native Nullstellensatz box lemma to the B+1 distinct integer values in ℂ. This argument allows complex coefficients and does not assume that the pulled-back minor has integer coefficients. The house estimate follows from parameterTuple_house.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: A nonzero first-jet minor survives the invertible embeddings parameter change and an inclusive bounded integer grid provides a nonvanishing specialization.

nodes.title: Degree-bounded evaluation surjectivity
nodes.statement: For κ produced by parameterJetChoice, degree-≤d evaluation ℚ[x₁,…,xᵣ]≤d→K is surjective, and the unrestricted ℚ-algebra map aeval κ is surjective. After extension to ℂ, the value-kernel gradients surject onto ⊕τℂ^r. Consequently κ generates K over ℚ; no integral-surjectivity assertion is made.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use GI.1’s first-jet/value/gradient split, the embeddings identification K⊗ℂ≃ℂ^n and faithful extension of scalars to descend the full rank of the value map. Surjectivity of the degree-bounded map implies that of the full algebra map.
acceptance: K=ℚ(i), κ=2i gives rational generation although ℤ[2i]≠ℤ[i].

sources.match: Full first jets imply full value evaluation and the corresponding rational field map is a closed immersion on spectra; the native jet split makes the gradient conclusion precise.

nodes.title: Integral bounded evaluation
nodes.statement: In GI.0 coefficient coordinates, Vℤ=ℤ^𝓜 with 𝓜={a∈ℕ^r:Σaⱼ≤d}, define the ℤ-linear map ε(c)=Σa cₐκ^a into 𝓞 K. It is exactly native aeval on MvPolynomial.restrictTotalDegree, transported along GI.0’s coefficient equivalence.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Evaluate each monomial in the native ring of integers and extend ℤ-linearly. Use the supplied coefficient equivalence, rather than define a second bounded polynomial type.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The degree-bounded integer evaluation map into the ring of integers is the map whose kernel and transpose enter the volume estimate.

nodes.title: Saturated relation lattice
nodes.statement: Define Lκ,d=ker ε as a native ℤ-submodule of Vℤ. Give its real span W the Euclidean inner product making the admissible monomials orthonormal, and give L its intrinsic covolume in W. Once εℚ is onto, rankℤL=M−n=ℓ and W=ker εℝ. Saturated means that for a≠0 in ℤ, ac∈L implies c∈L.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native linear-map kernel. Saturation follows from torsion-freeness of 𝓞 K. Rational evaluation has rank n; scalar extension commutes with this kernel. Embed coefficient vectors in the Euclidean space of dimension M, restricting measure to W; never take ambient M-dimensional volume of a lower-rank lattice.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The integral relation lattice is the intersection of the real evaluation kernel with the monomial coefficient lattice, of rank M−n.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_mem
api.statement: c∈L iff ε(c)=0.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_saturated

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_rank

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_zeroTuple

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_constant

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.relationLattice_scaledQuadratic

uses.how: Use saturation in the unimodular orthogonal-covolume identity.
Apply intrinsic Euclidean successive minima to its full real span.

nodes.title: Transpose evaluation image
nodes.statement: Define Dκ,d in Vℤ to be the image of Homℤ(𝓞 K,ℤ) under f↦(f(κ^a))a. This is the native dual evaluation map followed by the coefficient dot-product identification Vℤ≃Vℤ∨. It is contained in L⊥ℤ=W⊥∩Vℤ; once εℚ is onto both have rank n and D has finite index q=[L⊥ℤ:D]≥1.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use LinearMap.dualMap and GI.0’s monomial coefficient pairing. Every relation is annihilated. The rational transpose has rank n, so the two integral lattices have the same span and a finite positive relative index.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The dual of the ring of integers maps into the orthogonal integral lattice, without an assertion of equality; the node retains the finite-index comparison.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.transposeImage_mem
api.statement: v∈D iff there is f:Homℤ(𝓞 K,ℤ) with vₐ=f(κ^a).

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.transposeImage_orthogonal
api.statement: For v∈D and c∈L, Σa vₐcₐ=0.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.transposeImage_finiteIndex
api.statement: If εℚ is onto then [L⊥ℤ:D] is a positive finite integer; equality of D with L⊥ℤ is not presumed.

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.transposeImage_rational
tests.statement: For K=ℚ,κ=2,d=1, D=ℤ(1,2) and annihilates ℤ(−2,1).

tests.name: NumberField.CompactModel.transposeImage_constant
tests.statement: For K=ℚ,d=0, D is the full one-coordinate integer lattice.

uses.how: Compare its volume to the orthogonal lattice with the positive finite index q.
Compute its volume using an actual integral basis and the embeddings Gram matrix.

nodes.title: Finite-index discriminant identity
nodes.statement: Assume εℚ is onto. In any actual integral basis b of 𝓞 K, let B be the n×M integer coordinate matrix of ε and Aτ,a=τ(κ^a). Then q² covol(L)² = covol(D)² = det(B Bᵀ) = det(A A*)/|disc K|, where q=[L⊥ℤ:D]. All determinants on the right are real and positive, and A* is conjugate transpose. The covolumes use intrinsic coefficient Euclidean measure.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: GN.0’s primitive orthogonal-covolume theorem applies to the saturated kernel inside the unimodular coefficient lattice. Regard D and L⊥ℤ as full lattices in their common real span W⊥ with its intrinsic Euclidean measure. The general inner-product-space covolume/index theorem gives covol(D)=q covol(L⊥ℤ)=q covol(L), not a ratio of lower-rank ambient volumes.

Gram determinants compute the transpose image volume. Write A=T B using the embeddings matrix T of the actual integral basis b. The native discr_eq_basisMatrix_det_sq is stated for the canonical integral basis; a unimodular integral change of basis, with determinant ±1, gives |det T|²=|disc K| for b. Taking determinants of A A*=T(B Bᵀ)T* gives the stated identity. Rational surjectivity makes B full row rank and its Gram determinant positive.
acceptance: For κ=2i,d=1 the identity reads 4=16/4; omitting the index or treating α as an integral basis fails.

sources.match: The integral-basis change relates the transpose Gram determinant to the embeddings Gram determinant divided by absolute discriminant; the consumer keeps the intervening index explicitly.

nodes.title: Relation covolume bound
nodes.statement: For bounded full-jet κ let C=(n²d(r+1))^d δ^(2d) and D₀=M C². Then covol(L)≤D₀^(n/2)/√|disc K|≤D₀^(n/2). In particular all embedding evaluation entries are≤C in modulus. The coefficient Euclidean metric is unrelated to the supremum metric used to find α.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Bound each monomial using degree≤d and n²d(r+1)δ²≥1. Every diagonal entry of A A* is≤M C². Apply Hermitian Gram Hadamard, then finiteIndexGram with q≥1 and |disc K|≥1.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: Monomial evaluation height and Hadamard bound the relation covolume by D₀^(n/2), with the discriminant denominator retained in the stronger form.

nodes.title: Truncated short relations
nodes.statement: Set ℓ=M−n and k=ℓ+1−n. Under d≥5,r≥1,M≥n(r+1), ℓ≥nr≥1 and k≥r. There are ℓ independent integral relations Eᵢ ordered by coefficient ℓ² norm, with each norm≥1, product≤ℓ^(ℓ/2)D₀^(n/2). Retaining exactly the first k gives norm and every coefficient≤H₀=ℓ^(ℓ/(2n))√M(n²d(r+1))^dδ^(2d). Their span has codimension n−1 in the full relation space.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply GN.1’s intrinsic Euclidean ball lower bound and second theorem in W, then its genuine simultaneous minimum witnesses. Integral nonzero coefficient vectors have norm≥1. The ordered-product root bound has denominator ℓ−i; for zero-based i<k this is≥n. Independence gives precisely the asserted codimension.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The intrinsic Euclidean ball estimate and second minima bound allow discarding the largest n−1 relations and bound the retained coefficients.

nodes.title: A full-rank gradient block
nodes.statement: Let J:Lℂ→⊕τℂ^r be the surjective gradient map and U the span of the k retained relations, of codimension n−1. There is one embedding τ for which the projection J(U)→ℂ^r is onto. This assertion does not say that every block is automatically onto by dimension alone.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: The image J(U) has codimension at most n−1. If every block projection were deficient, choose a nonzero covector on each of the n blocks vanishing on that projection. These block-supported covectors are independent and annihilate J(U), forcing codimension≥n.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: Codimension n−1 of the retained relation span forces one full cotangent block.

nodes.title: A common nonzero Jacobian minor
nodes.statement: Choose r of the retained integral relations whose gradient determinant is nonzero at the full-rank embedding point. For these same r equations, J(κ)=det(∂Eᵢ/∂xⱼ(κ)) is a nonzero element of K and τ(J(κ))≠0 for every embedding τ. Their degrees are≤d and their coefficients are≤H₀.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Select an r×r minor of the one full-rank block. Evaluation and formal partial derivatives commute with embeddings, so it equals the image of one element of K. Injectivity of any field embedding propagates nonvanishing of that same determinant. No assumption that K is Galois and no independent choices of minors at different embeddings are needed.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: A selected gradient minor at one embedding is nonzero at every embedding; the proof here uses injectivity on its single field-valued determinant.

nodes.title: Jacobian-open arithmetic models
nodes.statement: For an ordered r-tuple E of integer polynomials in r variables, base change coefficients to ℚ, form R=ℚ[x]/(E₁,…,Eᵣ), and define A_E=R[J_E^−1] using native Ideal.Quotient and Localization.Away. J_E is the determinant of the formal derivative matrix. This is the coordinate algebra of the Jacobian-open part, and can be the zero ring.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Specialize SF.0’s native Jacobian localization; quotient by the actual ideal of equations and localize at the actual determinant. It is finite étale over ℚ. For a generating κ annihilating E with J_E(κ)≠0, the quotient and localization universal properties give a unique surjective ℚ-algebra map A_E→K.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The scheme defined by the equations with its Jacobian determinant inverted is the smooth zero-dimensional model; the node gives its native coordinate algebra.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.modelAlgebra_finiteEtale
api.statement: A_E is finite-dimensional and étale over ℚ, allowing the zero algebra.

api.name: NumberField.CompactModel.modelAlgebra_lift

Enumerate every field component of a fixed tuple, permitting multiple components.

nodes.title: Explicit compact model bound
nodes.statement: For every degree-n number field K, r≥1,d≥5,M=choose(d+r,d)≥n(r+1), and ℓ=M−n, there exist r integer polynomials of total degree≤d and coefficient absolute value≤ℓ^(ℓ/(2n))√M(n²d(r+1))^dδ^(2d), and a surjective ℚ-algebra map A_E→K. Thus Spec K is one irreducible component of the finite étale Jacobian-open model.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Combine shortIntegers, parameterJetChoice, saturated relations, the truncated minima bound and commonMinor. Use evaluationSurjective and modelAlgebra_lift to get the quotient map to K; constants and the generating tuple ensure surjectivity. Apply the field-factor API from SF.0.
acceptance: The coefficient bound is the exact Proposition 2 expression, not an asymptotic replacement.
The presentation describes K as a component over ℚ, not 𝓞 K as an integral quotient.

sources.match: Proposition 2 supplies the exact multivariate coefficient bound and the field as one irreducible component of the Jacobian-open scheme.

nodes.title: Least central-binomial parameter
nodes.statement: For n≥1 define r(n) as the least positive integer r satisfying n(r+1)≤choose(2r,r), and put d(n)=r(n). For a total natural-number API set r(0)=1. Existence follows from exponential growth; the eventual model theorem still requires n large enough that r(n)≥5.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: The lower bound choose(2r,r)≥2^r implies that choose(2r,r)/(r+1) tends to infinity. Choose the least positive witness, not an arbitrary large parameter.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The smallest positive central-binomial-capacity parameter is chosen with d=r.

nodes.title: Effective central-binomial estimates
nodes.statement: With n≥65536, L=log n, r=r(n), M=choose(2r,r), ℓ=M−n, we have 5≤r≤3L, n(r+1)≤M<4n(r+1)≤16nL, ℓ/(2n)≤8L, log M and log ℓ≤3L, and log(r(r+1))≤2L. For δ≥1, the explicit coefficient bound with d=r is≤(nδ)^(40L).
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Take r₀=ceil(2L/log2). Since r₀≥6 and r₀+1≤2^(r₀/2), choose(2r₀,r₀)≥2^r₀≥n(r₀+1); hence r≤r₀≤3L. Minimality and the ratio of consecutive choose(2r,r)/(r+1), strictly below 4, give M<4n(r+1). Elementary logarithmic inequalities at L≥log65536 give the displayed estimates. The four logarithmic contributions to the height are at most 24L², 1.5L, 12L² and 6L logδ, absorbed by 40L²+40L logδ.
acceptance: r(1)=1 prevents claiming d≥5 uniformly in all degrees.

nodes.title: Uniform logarithmic-size models
nodes.statement: There is one absolute constant Q=65536 such that every degree n≥Q number field admits r,d≤Q log n, M≤Qn log n and r integer equations of degree≤d with all coefficients≤(nδ)^(Q log n), whose Jacobian-open model contains Spec K as an irreducible component. The stronger choices d=r=r(n) and height≤(nδ)^(40 log n) are retained for counting.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Apply explicitModel with the least central parameter and use centralEstimates. Increasing the exponent from 40 to Q is valid since nδ≥1. The same constant Q is used for threshold, parameter and height bounds.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

nodes.title: Finite equation coefficient boxes
nodes.statement: For natural r,d,B, define the set ℬ(r,d,B) of ordered r-tuples of native integer polynomials whose total degrees are≤d and every coefficient has absolute value≤B. Equivalently it is the product of rM copies of the integer interval [−B,B], using GI.0’s coefficient coordinates. Zero polynomials and zero equations are included.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the native bounded-degree submodule and the supplied coefficient equivalence. The interval is inclusive and B is a natural number.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

nodes.title: Exact coefficient enumeration
nodes.statement: The unweighted cardinality of ℬ(r,d,B) is (2B+1)^(r·choose(d+r,d)). If a real height bound F≥0 bounds integer coefficients, membership is exactly the bound B=⌊F⌋₊; the floor must be preserved before counting.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: The coefficient equivalence makes the box a finite product of rM copies of [−B,B], each of size 2B+1. Use coefficientBox_floor for the equivalence between a nonnegative real height and its natural floor. No sparsity, monicity or nonsingularity filter is assumed.
acceptance: At r=1,d=0,B=1 the exact count is 3; replacing 2B+1 by 2B loses the zero choice.

nodes.title: Isomorphism classes of model components
nodes.statement: Use ST.0’s embedded finite extensions in ℚbar and its quotient by ℚ-algebra isomorphism. For a finite-dimensional commutative ℚ-algebra A and a maximal ideal p, send p to the class of the residue field A/p, embedded in ℚbar by any ℚ-embedding. This class is independent of that embedding. Apply it to A_E; no weight by automorphisms or embeddings is attached.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: A maximal quotient of a finite-dimensional ℚ-algebra is a finite number field and embeds in ℚbar. The chosen embedded copy has a well-defined ST.0 quotient class because any two copies are ℚ-isomorphic. Characterize the class through any surjective algebra map with kernel p.
acceptance: Establish the stated bound or equivalence with the exact constants, ranks and inclusive inequalities.

sources.match: The proof observes that several number fields can appear in one model; taking their rational isomorphism classes gives the correct unweighted covering map.

nodes.title: Isolated-component Bézout bound
nodes.statement: For r≥1 and r equations of degrees≤d over ℚ, the number of maximal ideals of their Jacobian-open algebra is finite and≤d^r. More precisely after extension to an algebraic closure its isolated local lengths sum to≤the product of positive equation degrees≤d^r; each Jacobian-open geometric point is simple. Other components of the whole zero locus may have positive dimension. A zero equation or constant nonzero equation yields an empty Jacobian-open part.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the requested SF.5 arbitrary-dimensional isolated-intersection bound after homogenizing in projective r-space. Restrict to affine isolated points and use the nonzero determinant to give local length 1. Finite étale factors each contribute at least one geometric point, so the component count is no larger. Handle zero or constant equations separately before using positive degrees.
acceptance: Do not replace this by SF.5’s two-plane-curve result when r>2.
The line-only example (xy,x(y−1)) has zero Jacobian-open components.

sources.match: The intersection-number argument bounds the isolated points even in a zero locus with other components; the generic arbitrary-dimensional theorem remains an explicit SF.5 input.

nodes.title: Bounded models cover field classes
nodes.statement: For n≥65536 and real H≥1, put r=d=r(n), M=choose(2r,r), F=(n H^(1/n))^(40 log n), B=⌊F⌋₊. The disjoint union, over E∈ℬ(r,d,B), of maximal ideals of A_E maps by componentClass onto ST.0’s unweighted set of exact-degree-n ℚ-isomorphism classes with |disc|≤H, after restricting the domain to components satisfying that cutoff. Its domain cardinality is at most (2B+1)^(rM)d^r.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: For every field in the cutoff, δ≤H^(1/n); uniformModel in its stronger 40-exponent form supplies a tuple in the box and a surjective map A_E→K. Its kernel maps to the required class. Bound all components in the full finite union by isolatedComponents and coefficientBoxCard. Do not select an injective map from field classes to equation tuples.
acceptance: Multiple fields can share an equation tuple; the factor d^r accounts for this.
Different embedded copies or multiple equal residue factors count a class once.

sources.match: The small-model theorem covers the cutoff by component models; counting all components rather than one tuple per field supplies the multiplicity factor.

nodes.title: Degree-sensitive field count
nodes.statement: For the same absolute Q=65536, every integer n≥Q and real H≥1 satisfy Nₙ(H)≤n^(Q n (log n)^3) H^(Q (log n)^3), where Nₙ(H) is the ordinary cardinality of exact-degree-n number fields up to ℚ-isomorphism with |disc|≤H. The bound is inclusive, unweighted and uniform in both variables.
hypotheses: Global conventions in the reader apply; every additional hypothesis is included in the statement.
proofSteps: Retain the finite bound (2floor₊F+1)^(rM)d^r. With L=log n use rM≤48nL², logF=40L²+(40L/n)logH, log(2floor₊F+1)≤log3+logF, and log(d^r)≤3L². The logarithm of the finite bound is≤2000nL⁴+1920L³logH, which is≤QnL⁴+QL³logH. Exponentiate; the n-power has exponent QnL³. ST.0 supplies the carrier and baseline Hermite finiteness, not this asymptotic estimate.

For the finiteness bridge, ST.0’s isoFamily is the quotient image of the finite fixed-ambient embedded family. For real H≥1 use the integer cutoff floor₊H, then restrict to degree n and take the quotient image. This imports ST.0’s Northcott argument and the existing explicit Hermite infrastructure rather than defining another arithmetic family.
acceptance: At H=1 the H-factor is 1; no logH division occurs.
n=1 is outside the asserted threshold; no false r≥5 claim follows.
No dependence on ArithmeticStatistics:ST.3, nor any algorithmic runtime claim.
